summary: Both deliverables are acceptable. The code change replaces the greenlet stack-switching batcher with an ordinary synchronous generator in callback_stream.py: transitions are serialized into a deque by a sink installed on run.proxy_events, next(iterator) is only called when the deque is empty, and queued records are then emitted in acquisition order under the retained per-batch record/byte/selected-event limits with the one-oversized-record allowance. Selected-event destination routing (batch split on destination change, transitions riding with the current destination, steps dict only for MPI) is preserved. Cleanup is correct in all paths I traced: normal exhaustion closes the iterator after draining; GeneratorExit from close() and callback exceptions both close the iterator, which clears the sink (pending and partial records) and closes the owned input exactly once; cleanup failures do not mask the primary callback error. The documented limitation that close() cannot interrupt a running callback on the same thread is accurate. CallbackIterator is unchanged in behavior; its drain_remaining path still forwards remaining transitions to the sink before closing input, and the serial (SmdReaderManager) and MPI (CallbackEventBuilderManager, chunks() finally drains the SMD0 terminator) integrations are unchanged from the base. pyproject.toml declares no greenlet; the only remaining greenlet mentions are conda lock files unrelated to this package, historical notes, and the forbidding import hook in run_callback_stream.py. Tests: the stress driver now asserts the whole callback finishes before the first batch arrives (accurate delayed-delivery characterization) while keeping bounded-output, oversized-record, close-early, before-start and failure coverage; test_callback_stream.py retains serial/MPI select/reject/return x destinations, metadata, step counts, early-return drain, and MPI routing checks. Case counts (24 + 18 + 17 = 59) match the supplied focused evidence, and the supplied final-SHA core and byhand runs pass with no xfails. Issue payload: title carries the psana2-cpu prefix, labels are bug plus psana2-cpu with a valid proposed color, the body correctly describes delayed-not-lost transitions, unbounded pending memory, the no-yield/reject-all cases, references the correct greenlet commit SHA, names existing test files, states no production OOM/loss incident, does not pre-authorize any dependency or API change, and keeps the counter fix out of scope. Superseded step-3 and root README records are marked historical. One low, non-blocking documentation nit.
